verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time, ... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'splashed down ... Pacific Ocean ... 8:07 p.m. ET'; R3: '8:07 p.m. ET in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California'; R4: '8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm exact date, time, timezone conversion, location, and Pacific Ocean.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule landed approximately 40 to 50 miles from the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly states the exact distance range and location.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams were stationed to retrieve the Artemis II astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery team took more than an hour to approach'; R2: 'recovery teams ... approaching Orion'; R3: 'Navy divers ... recovery vessel'; R4: 'NASA and U.S. military recovery team will be standing by'
verifications.reasoning: All primary sources detail recovery teams positioned for astronaut retrieval post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: Artemis II was a flyby mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'moon flyby'; R2: 'flyby of the Moon'; R4: 'historic lunar flyby'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe Artemis II as a lunar flyby mission.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown method was parachute-assisted splashdown of the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'parachute-assisted splashdown'; R4: 'drogue parachutes ... three main parachutes ... splash down'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm parachute deployment sequence leading to Orion capsule splashdown.

verifications.claim: Future Artemis missions (Artemis III and beyond) are targeting the lunar South Pole.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis III will ... remain in orbit around Earth'; 'Artemis IV ... land on the moon near the moon’s south pole'; R6: 'Artemis III ... low-Earth orbit'; R7: 'Artemis III ... near the South Pole'; R8: 'Artemis IV ... near the South Pole'
verifications.reasoning: Sources contradict on Artemis III (Earth orbit vs. South Pole plans); later missions target South Pole.
